rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources required with notice to quit or non-renewal
rules.requirement: If your Boston landlord (or a foreclosing owner) serves you a Notice to Quit or a notice that your lease won't be renewed, they must give you a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time, and send a copy of the notice to the City's Office of Housing Stability. If you don't get it, report it to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity (617-635-2500 or 311). A violation does not stop the eviction.
rules.key_value: Tenant rights notice must be served with the Notice to Quit or non-renewal; fines of $300/day for second and later offenses
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston. Covers evictions, lease non-renewals, and occupants asked to leave after foreclosure. Tenants cannot waive these rights.
rules.exemptions: Residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities; non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.
rules.citation: City of Boston Ordinances, Housing Stability Notification Act (Sec. 10-11.7)
rules.quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.
rules.penalty: Enforced by the Inspectional Services Department: warning for a 1st offense; $300 per day for 2nd and later offenses. A violation does not halt the eviction process.

notes: The HSNA is a notice/disclosure requirement attached to notices to quit and lease non-renewals. It does not limit the reasons a landlord can end a tenancy. I filed it under just_cause_eviction because that category covers eviction notice rules, but it is borderline: it could also count as excluded notice-to-quit procedure. Confidence is lowered for that reason. Citation: the FAQ labels the penalty schedule 'Sec. 10-11.7'. The full ordinance section may be cited differently. The ordinance passed in October 2020 and took effect November 6, 2020. No rules on rent caps, deposits, fees, screening or algorithmic pricing appear in this document.
